title: Certificates of Deposit: recovering the tier's standard rate at the start of a term for a penalty check
content:
## Scope

When the rate the charter fixes for a Certificates of Deposit term is worked out in order to check an early withdrawal penalty, the tier's standard rate at the start of that term is not looked up in today's rate card; it is recovered from the certificate itself. This rule states how.

## Rule

The tier's standard rate at term start is taken as the certificate's interest rate, less the tier's jumbo bonus points when the certificate is marked as carrying the jumbo bonus, and less the tier's relationship bonus points when the certificate is marked as carrying the relationship bonus.

## Condition table

| Jumbo bonus marked on the certificate | Relationship bonus marked on the certificate | Standard rate at term start |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Interest rate, less jumbo points, less relationship points |
| Yes | No | Interest rate, less jumbo points |
| No | Yes | Interest rate, less relationship points |
| No | No | The interest rate itself |

## Worked example (hypothetical figures, not tier values)

A certificate shows an interest rate of 4.30 percent and is marked as carrying both bonuses; its tier's hypothetical jumbo points are 0.10 and relationship points 0.20.

- Standard rate at term start: 4.30, less 0.10, less 0.20, gives 4.00 percent.
- Had only the jumbo bonus been marked: 4.30, less 0.10, gives 4.20 percent.

## Points of judgement

**Is the current published standard rate used instead?**
No. The standard rate at term start is recovered from the certificate's own interest rate and bonus markers, as above.

**Which bonus points are taken off?**
Only those of a bonus the certificate is marked as carrying, and at the tier's bonus points for that bonus.
